title: Google Calendar, Mirrored Server-Side, No Browser Needed | vitalii.no
description:
Google Calendar events reached the family's web app only through the browser's own login token, so they existed nowhere on the server — a device that never signed in to Google, like the kitchen TV kiosk, could never see them. Worse, four brothers play football under the same club group, so an event titled just "Fotballtrening" couldn't be attributed to any one child by title alone.

The server now subscribes to the calendar's own secret iCal address and mirrors it every 15 minutes into its own database table, kept separate from the web app's existing events so nothing doubles up in the grid. A hand-written parser unfolds the feed, resolves time zones and all-day dates, and expands recurring events inside a rolling window. Children are assigned the same way the web app already does — keyword rules first, then a name match — and a refinement lets a whole feed belong to one child outright, so when the same training shows up in both a shared calendar and a tagged one, the system keeps the copy that actually knows whose child it is.

The TV kiosk can finally see the family's Google Calendar events at all, and four brothers' football no longer collapses into one unattributed entry — each child's own feed answers "whose training is this?" outright, surviving even the club renaming the group between seasons.
